candidates.spoken: Why Earth's core matches the Sun's surface heat.
What If You Could Touch Earth's Core?
Yet the inner core is a solid iron ball.
Crushing pressure keeps the metal from melting.
A solid iron ball as hot as the Sun's surface.
It would not all happen at once.
Touching it is impossible; no material survives the trip.
Its radius is about 1,230 kilometres, 70% of the Moon's.
So pressure, not heat alone, decides whether rock is solid.
In 2005, shear waves were detected passing through it.

script.spoken: Why Earth's core matches the Sun's surface heat. Its surface is about 5,700 kelvin. Yet the inner core is a solid iron ball. Crushing pressure keeps the metal from melting. Its radius is about 1,230 kilometres, 70% of the Moon's. In 2005, shear waves were detected passing through it. Touching it is impossible; no material survives the trip. So pressure, not heat alone, decides whether rock is solid.
